verdicts.quote: Automatic, first-come-first-served promotion is the proposed product default. ... For each admission, create an ordinary confirmed booking and end its active entry as **Promoted** as one business outcome.

Simultaneous joins by distinct members acquire a unique order as accepted by the booking authority, even when timestamps coincide. ... Manual queue overrides, special priority tiers, timed offers, penalties ... are outside this scope.
Promotion uses the existing booking identity and terms. ... Manual queue overrides, special priority tiers, timed offers, penalties, and a new outbound notification system are outside this scope.
verdicts.missing: Whether a member auto-promoted without noticing who then no-shows or late-cancels incurs the existing no-show/late-cancellation penalty; the existing policy is unrecovered and no-shows are not addressed.

verdicts.quote: If the availability change can complete without immediate allocation, its effect must be recoverable without either member's client ... A fresh read shows **Booked** ... even if the member's app was closed.
verdicts.missing: Timeliness of the background allocation: NFR says recovery and availability targets are unresolved and no maximum delay is promised.

verdicts.quote: Add private, recoverable in-app waitlist outcomes through the class and member booking surfaces. ... No live update is required between authoritative reads ... outbound notifications, and delivery receipts for messages are inapplicable

Duplicate or stale release processing cannot issue extra bookings, reuse a released seat, re-promote a terminal entry ... A valid allocation may bring confirmed use exactly to capacity, never above it.

An ordinary booking competing for a released seat can succeed only after the eligible queue receives its priority and capacity remains. Simultaneous leaves, releases, bookings, and closure resolve in one authoritative order for the occurrence.
verdicts.missing: What happens specifically when the waitlisted member themself books directly while being promoted (only the head's Leave racing promotion and other members' bookings are specified).

verdicts.quote: If an ordinary booking requires a fresh member choice, payment authorization, or terms acceptance, automatic promotion for that class type is unready. Product must settle whether the necessary consent can be collected on Join
verdicts.missing: When payment is taken for a promoted booking and what happens if it fails.

verdicts.quote: The request supplies no active-entry count limit. If the runtime needs one, product must decide the applicable bound and the Join behavior at it before that path is planned.
verdicts.missing: Whether there is a waitlist cap, its value, and what a member sees when the waitlist is full.

verdicts.quote: The effective waitlist cutoff is the earlier of any ordinary booking cutoff and the scheduled start. ... Stop at the cutoff even if seats remain. ... At the cutoff and later it cannot.

Cancellation of a confirmed booking, a capacity increase ... serves the earliest still-eligible entries first. ... Existing bookings are not displaced to create a seat. If the baseline permits an over-capacity state through a capacity decrease, promotion stops
On occurrence cancellation, end them with **Class canceled**. Clear rank and remove the actionable Join and Leave controls for ended entries.

Reads derive current rank from committed active order. ... Rank is a derived value and loses its meaning at termination. ... Left, Promoted, Ineligible, Waitlist closed and Class canceled are terminal entry outcomes
Cleanup removes expired terminal and replay information under the existing retention and deletion policy.
verdicts.missing: How long terminal waitlist entries are kept after the class runs; retention is listed as an open bound.

verdicts.quote: A current authorized read shows the member's one-based rank among active entries. ... no read exposes another member's identity.
Manual queue overrides ... are outside this scope. ... No new scheduling or staff administration capabilities are in scope. ... Operational access stays within existing roles and purpose.
verdicts.missing: Whether staff can view a class's waitlist and a history of who was promoted when; manual promote/remove is excluded but staff visibility is not defined.

verdicts.quote: The recovery and availability targets are unresolved. Booking engineering must establish the current operating and recovery envelopes before choosing a mechanism or promising a maximum delay.
verdicts.missing: The actual bound on time from cancellation to promotion.

verdicts.quote: Below capacity, normal booking applies subject to R-3. ... Existing bookings are not displaced to create a seat.
